result.instructor_feedback:
You’re building a solid “glass box → roof carve” workflow! The strongest part of your submission is that the concept views genuinely expose your thinking: you’re boxing the mass, finding midlines, and using guides to place the ridge and roof planes before committing to contour—exactly the right habit for reliable perspective. In the top set, the roof construction reads well, but the scaffolding gets visually noisy, and a few guide families feel like they’re drifting (some depth lines don’t convincingly converge to the same VP, and a couple of verticals lean slightly, which weakens the sense of a stable box). Where we need to pivot: reduce scaffolding clutter and tighten perspective coherence. Keep each construction phase in a distinct line weight (very light for guides, medium for box, darker for final roof edges) so the structural logic reads instantly.

This tells us the construction scaffolding isn't yet doing its job — it's generating lines, but not locking in a consistent 3D model that you can rotate mentally and re-draw from a new angle. Where we need to pivot: Stop adding more vanishing lines and instead slow down to verify each one. Before drawing the roof peak, ask yourself: where does this point sit in 3D space relative to the box below it? Use your bounding box — the roof peak should sit at a measurable, consistent height above the top face of the rectangular volume in every view. Also, in your bottom-row presentation view, the construction lines are still dominating; the 'clean' version needs a much more decisive line weight contrast — press harder on your final contour lines or use a separate sheet so the scaffolding physically cannot bleed through. Your Next Step: Take just one of your four sketches — the top-right presentation view, which is your strongest — and redraw it on a fresh sheet. This time, first draw only the bounding box of the rectangular volume in light lines, then locate the roof ridge point at the center-top of the box's front face, then draw the four roof planes. Once that's clean, flip to a new sheet and attempt the same house from your bottom-left viewpoint using the *exact same* proportional decisions (same wall height, same roof pitch). Place the two sheets side by side and check: does the roof look like it belongs to the same building? That comparison will immediately reveal where your spatial model needs reinforcement.
